diagnostics.message: `helm_release.karpenter` declares `depends_on = [null_resource.wait_for_cluster]`, but it already depends on `null_resource.wait_for_cluster` transitively: it references `module.karpenter` (via service_account/queue_name), which has `depends_on = [null_resource.patch_calico_installation]`, which implicitly depends on `data.external.update_kubeconfig`, which has `depends_on = [null_resource.wait_for_cluster]`. The explicit depends_on adds no ordering and is redundant.

The Karpenter controller installed by `helm_release.karpenter` relies on EKS Pod Identity to obtain IAM credentials — `module.karpenter` is configured with `create_pod_identity_association = true`. Pod Identity credentials are only delivered by the EKS Pod Identity Agent daemon, which is installed by `aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent`. Nothing orders the controller after that addon (they only share transitive prerequisites), so Karpenter pods may start before the agent is running and fail to authenticate. `helm_release.karpenter` should depend on `aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent`.
